items.followUp: Define an unsaturated solution and give an example.

rubric.why: Defines supersaturation by comparing the amount of dissolved solute with a saturated solution at the same temperature.
rubric.description: Correct definition of a supersaturated solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it contains more dissolved solute than a saturated solution at the same temperature.

rubric.why: Gives a suitable example of a supersaturated solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a hot saturated sugar solution cooled carefully without crystallization.

modelAnswer: A supersaturated solution contains more dissolved solute than a saturated solution at the same temperature.
Example: A hot saturated sugar solution, cooled carefully without crystallization, is supersaturated.

items.followUp: Write balanced equations for the reactions of chlorine with hydrogen and with cold, dilute sodium hydroxide.

rubric.why: Shows the balanced substitution reaction of methane with a halogen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct balanced equation, such as CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl.

rubric.why: States the condition for the methane–halogen substitution reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that sunlight or ultraviolet light is required.

rubric.why: Shows the balanced reaction of chlorine with sodium hydroxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation producing sodium chloride and sodium hypochlorite.

rubric.why: Identifies the conditions for the sodium hypochlorite reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the sodium hydroxide is cold and dilute.

modelAnswer: Methane reacts with chlorine in sunlight by substitution: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl.
With cold, dilute sodium hydroxide: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaOCl + H₂O.

items.followUp: Explain how a cation differs from an anion.

accept: equal numbers of protons and electrons
rubric.why: States that an atom is neutral because it has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons and is electrically neutral.

rubric.why: Distinguishes an ion from an atom by its charge and the gain or loss of electrons.
rubric.description: Difference in charge and electron transfer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an ion is a charged atom formed by gaining or losing electrons.

modelAnswer: An atom is electrically neutral because it has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
An ion is a charged atom formed when it gains or loses electrons.

items.followUp: Why does atomic radius decrease across a period and increase down a group?

accept: attraction for bonding electrons becomes stronger
rubric.why: Explains that increasing nuclear charge across a period strengthens attraction for bonding electrons, increasing electronegativity.
rubric.description: Reason electronegativity increases across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting increasing nuclear charge and little change in shielding with stronger attraction for bonding electrons.

accept: number of shells and shielding increase
rubric.why: Explains that added shells and increased shielding down a group weaken the attraction for bonding electrons, decreasing electronegativity.
rubric.description: Reason electronegativity decreases down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting increased distance and shielding down a group with weaker attraction for bonding electrons.

modelAnswer: Across a period, nuclear charge increases while shielding changes little, so the attraction for bonding electrons becomes stronger and electronegativity increases.
Down a group, the number of shells and shielding increase, so bonding electrons are farther from the nucleus and electronegativity decreases.
